classification.difficultyReason: Earlier parts explicitly scaffold angles, exact trigonometric lengths and an AAA similarity/proportional-side argument. The final part still requires recognising the perpendicular endpoint triangle and combining remaining walking-path lengths with Pythagoras; that routine linked synthesis puts the whole task just into Mastery.

content.prompt:
Pedro and Sam are both camping in the bush. Sam’s campsite is 15 km due east of Pedro’s campsite. At 9 a.m., they both walk out from their campsites. Initially Pedro walks 5 km to checkpoint $A$. From there, he turns right $90^\circ$ and walks 15 km to checkpoint $B$. Sam just walks 10 km to checkpoint $C$. The paths Pedro and Sam follow from their campsites are indicated on the diagram below. The angles are given from due north. Let $P$ and $S$ represent Pedro and Sam’s campsites, respectively.

Let $X$ be the point where their paths cross and $Y$ be the point of intersection of the lines $PS$ and $AX$.

spec.description: Editable walking-path diagram. Ordinary paths and point markers use house black; red dashed compass and projection guides distinguish directional construction. The 150° sector at S runs anticlockwise from north to the southwest path. Coordinates derive from the supplied lengths and angles. Native angle and right-angle marks require final-size inspection.
spec.mathematics: PA perpendicular to AB; A,Y,X,B collinear; S,X,C collinear; P,Y,Z,S collinear; XZ perpendicular to PS. PA=5 km, AB=15 km, PS=15 km, SC=10 km are supplied in the stem, not labelled on the diagram.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied question geometry only; no calculated lengths or requested angles.

answer.worked: $\angle SYX=\angle AYP=30^\circ$ because they are vertically opposite angles.

The marked $150^\circ$ is anticlockwise from north, so $\angle XSY=150^\circ-90^\circ=60^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle SXY&=180^\circ-60^\circ-30^\circ\\\angle SXY&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle PAY$ and $\triangle SXY$ are similar.

answer.short: $\triangle PAY\sim\triangle SXY$ (AAA): corresponding angles are $60^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $30^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$\angle PAY=\angle SXY=90^\circ$.

$\angle APY=\angle XSY=60^\circ$.

$\angle AYP=\angle SYX=30^\circ$.

Therefore $\triangle PAY\sim\triangle SXY$ (AAA), with correspondence $P\leftrightarrow S$, $A\leftrightarrow X$, $Y\leftrightarrow Y$.

Using corresponding sides of $\triangle PAY$ and $\triangle SXY$:

$$\begin{align*}\frac{SX}{PA}&=\frac{SY}{PY}\\SX&=5\times\frac{5}{10}\\SX&=2.5\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

children.label: f
children.prompt: Hence, find how far apart Pedro and Sam finish up. Give your answer, correct to the nearest metre.

answer.short:
$7.765\text{ km}$, or $7765\text{ m}$.

Use Pythagoras’ theorem in right-angled $\triangle BXC$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}XC&=SC-SX\\XC&=10-2.5\\XC&=\frac{15}{2}\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

Since $\angle BXC=90^\circ$, Pythagoras’ theorem gives

$$\begin{align*}BC^2&=XB^2+XC^2\\BC^2&=\left(\frac{30-15\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)^2\\BC^2&=225(2-\sqrt3)\\BC&=15\sqrt{2-\sqrt3}\text{ km}\\BC&\approx7.765\text{ km}\end{align*}$$

Pedro and Sam finish $7765\text{ m}$ apart, to the nearest metre.
